newsitem.title: USA: HFS adding Value Rent-A-Car to its Avis acquisition.
newsitem.headline: HFS adding Value Rent-A-Car to its Avis acquisition.

text.p: HFS Inc., expanding its recent entry into the car rental business, said Monday it reached an agreement in principle to buy Value Rent-A-Car Inc. from Mitsubishi Motor Sales of America Inc. for $175 million in cash.
If the deal is completed, it would follow the October purchase of Avis Inc. by HFS, which also franchises hotels and real estate broker offices.
Value, which has a fleet of about 22,000 cars, serves mostly vacation customers from 45 corporate-owned rental car sites, primarily in Florida.
The deal will add Value's mostly leisure customers to Avis's big stable of business and corporate customers.

"We expect to offer Value franchises to existing Avis licensees, to Avis Rent a Car (Inc.), which is planned to become an independent public company during the third quarter of 1997, and to other rental car operators," HFS Vice Chairman Stephen P. Holmes said in a statement.
Avis, which HFS acquired for $800 million, is the second-biggest rental car company in the United States.

Value reported revenues of about $180 million last year, up from $150 million in 1995. HFS said it would add "marginally" to its profits this year and would make "a more significant" contribution next year.

HFS also said that it and Mitsubishi Motor Sales, a unit of Mitsubishi Motors Corp. of Japan, intend to enter into a vehicle supply agreement and related marketing agreements in connection with Value's continuing fleet purchases from Mitsubishi.
The company, which is based in Parsippany, N.J., said it expected the acquisition to be completed by the end of June, pending approval by the two comapnies' boards and by government regulators.
HFS's stock closed Friday at $68.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
